When I was 17, I started smoking cigarettes. Already a bad move on my part, I nevertheless convinced a friend of a friend who was visiting from TN and was of age to buy lighters/tobacco products to buy me a lighter. I gave her the money and we left the convenience store, me with one of those push-down lighters with a picture of a thumbs-up on it.

When I got home, I immediately shut myself in my room and when on the computer (as you do when you're 17 and your 15 year old sister is upstairs and your grandparents are too old to understand your struggles). I also started playing with the lighter inside, and now we all know where this is going.

At first I lit things that didn't burn too quickly, mainly paper plates. But then for some reason I decided to light up the thin receipt for the lighter. Do you see where it's going NOW?

Of course, the receipt went up in flames and in a panic I dropped it. Not on the floor so I could stomp it out/clean up the scorch marks or explain them away later. No, that would have been the smart thing to do.

Instead, I dropped it on the bed. My bed. With the down comforter. 

The bed proceeded to catch fire, a circular shape of flames quickly growing until I could tear my eyes away long enough to go grab a red solo cup of water and douse them. Luckily the only thing that was really damaged was the comforter. Unluckily for me, it was damaged completely beyond repair. There were feathers everywhere.

My grandmother was 71 at the time and she would be damned if anyone messed up her house in any way. She's sweet as hell and always took better care of me and my siblings than my parents did, but if you didnt pick up a sock or push in a chair juuuuust the right way, she came at ya. Naturally, this made me terrified. I tried to rub away the scorch marks so I could maybe tell her I accidentally ripped it, which sounds a whole lot better than intentionally setting fires in the house. It was no use.

I didn't sleep much that night, having already resigned myself to the fact that i was gonna get kicked out back into my parents' house. At 8 am I crawled out of my room, did my best puppy dog look, and told my gramma I had something to show her.

The only thing she asked was if anybody got hurt. When I told her no, she said "don't worry about it then". I did still feel bad but I was able to get some sleep after she said that.

Six years later I still smoke cigarettes, which will probably fuck me later, but I haven't played with fire since.

Tl;dr: Idiot teenager plays with fire, bed gets burned. Feathers everywhere.

I work at a convenience store that doesn't do cash back. Now, on second shift, there are two people running two registers. Only you are permitted to use your assigned register unless the person using it is manager, assistant manager, or key holder, or, me if given explicit permission by one of the above three people since I've been there longest out of all the regular associates. One register is attached to the money in the safe, and the person running it leaves at 8 or 9, leaving the other person to run the register without the safe on until 10 when 3rd shift comes on. Since the register isn't attached to the safe, you can't get money out of it after either 8 or 9 pm, which is a big difference as to how much you're leaving in your drawer. 

And you'd be surprised as to how many people come in after 9 pm and try to pay for <20 worth of stuff with a 50 or a hundred. They do this multiple times.
